startup.name: MochaCare
startup.one_liner: Agentic Management Service for Care Organizations
startup.description: MochaCare is an agentic management service for care organizations such as home care agencies. It handles hiring, scheduling and client intake end to end so partners can focus on growth. A team of two in San Francisco, Winter 2026 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: Blind test: the company is known to have been accepted, so this is a placeholder note and not a real estimate. The prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md), and this team would sit near the middle, helped by the AI agents theme within that range.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Not applicable in this test because the company was accepted. If YC had said no, the likely reasons would be a service heavy model that looks like an agency, unclear healthcare domain credentials, and crowded home care software from AlayaCare and WellSky.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry Healthcare --calibration-only gave seed 50% (n=22, CI 31-69%); python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B gave 59%.
anchors.adjustment_reason: At the Healthcare anchor and below the B2B anchor, because home care is a slow sector and a services model scales slowly.

bands.rationale: Small seed near the B2B 2022+ median of $3.2M, low side.
Typical seed on early agency revenue.
Upside if revenue per agency is high.
Thin round of angels and a small fund.

ladder.why_it_fails: The probable stop is that investors see a service business with low software margins and only a handful of care agency customers. Sage Care (S24), a close analog, had no priced round recorded, and Anchor Health (W16) shut down in home health. Healthcare takes a median of 19 months to seed in the data, so a round above $500K within 12 months is less than certain.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only gave series_a 26% given seed (n=74); Healthcare 2022-2025 gave 9% (n=11).
anchors.adjustment_reason: 0.77 times the B2B anchor, honoring the 0.75 floor while allowing for the much lower Healthcare cohort figure.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A fails if margins stay low because humans still run much of hiring and scheduling, and if care agencies are small and churn. Axle Health (W21) reached Series A selling software to the same buyers, but only after years, and Tivara (S24) shut down after a seed selling AI staff to medical groups.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2018-2022 --industry B2B --calibration-only gave series_b 35% given series_a (n=23); 2022-2025 gave 16%.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B fails when growth depends on hiring operations staff, so revenue scales linearly with headcount. Regulated care, wage pressure and high caregiver turnover of about 75% keep customers fragile, and software only rivals such as AlayaCare can undercut.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Below anchor for a vertical with few large buyers.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C fails if the company remains a regional managed service and is acquired by a home care software or private equity roll up for under $1B. Few care operations companies reach large independent rounds.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The most likely failure is that a two person team runs a human intensive service for a slow, price sensitive buyer and cannot reach software margins. Anchor Health shut down and Tivara failed after a seed, while ReverCare was acquired small.

analogs.relevance: AI automation for home care agencies, 2024.

killers.risk: A service model keeps margins low and growth tied to headcount
killers.evidence: The offer is an end to end managed service, which resembles staffing and operations outsourcing, not software.
killers.mitigation: Productize workflows and price per outcome.

killers.risk: Small, slow, price sensitive buyers in home care
killers.evidence: Home care agencies are numerous and small, with turnover near 75 percent per AlayaCare sources.
killers.mitigation: Start with a few mid size agencies and show cost savings.

killers.evidence: AlayaCare already markets AI for scheduling and burnout reduction.
killers.mitigation: Own outcomes like filled shifts and time to hire.

competition_now.name: AlayaCare
competition_now.what: Home care management software with AI features.
competition_now.traction: Established vendor marketing scheduling, billing and caregiver management.

competition_now.name: WellSky Personal Care
competition_now.what: Scheduling, EVV and billing for agencies.
competition_now.traction: Suited to large multi location agencies.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents for scheduling, screening candidates and intake are buildable by two engineers using existing models. The hard parts are integrations, compliance and reliability in real operations.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents with agency customers can add AI scheduling and intake in about a year, and other agent startups can copy the offer quickly.

evidence.claim: Home care turnover is around 75 percent and agencies spend heavily on hiring and scheduling.
Vendors sell scheduling software to agencies, showing paid demand.

actions: Run the service for three agencies.

roadmap.proof: About $20K monthly revenue and a seed above $500K.
Gross margin above 60 percent and $1M of annual revenue.

pros.evidence: Turnover around 75 percent makes hiring and scheduling costly for agencies.

pros.point: Agent technology is cheap to start
pros.evidence: Intake, screening and scheduling are buildable with current models by a small team.

brand.name: MochaCare
weaknesses: Mocha suggests coffee, not operations; generic Care suffix
brand.rationale: A warm, approachable name that suits care organizations, but the coffee word is unrelated and the Care suffix is common in health names. The effect is neutral.

narrative.headline: A real pain point, but a service heavy model in a slow vertical makes later rounds hard.
narrative.general_summary: MochaCare sells a managed agentic service for home care agencies, handling hiring, scheduling and intake. The pain is real because caregiver turnover is very high, but the buyers are small and slow, and healthcare cohorts take longer to reach seed and show a low Series A rate. A service model risks low margins, and incumbents such as AlayaCare are adding AI. A seed is roughly a coin flip within a year, with the Series A less likely than the B2B average. A pivot to pure software, or a roll up of agencies, is a plausible upside path, and paying customers can keep the company alive for years.

assumptions: Blind test using only the batch start description.
Healthcare cohort is small (n=22 and n=11 for A).
Seed means a round above $500K within about 12 months.
Coverage per knowledge/coverage.md: 662 of 6,399 companies researched.
